purpose: Inventory of the libraries vendored under thirdparty/ so that a future upgrade is 'fetch tarball, drop subset, rebuild' rather than archaeology. Verify with tools/vendor-check.py (classifies every tracked file as unmodified/patched/local and fails if the manifest disagrees). See UPGRADING.md for the recipe.
build: Each lib is a libtool noinst convenience archive built by thirdparty/Makefile.am (explicit _SOURCES lists, -fPIC, folded into libabinova). Upstream build systems are NOT vendored; on upgrade, refresh the _SOURCES list and _CPPFLAGS -I paths in Makefile.am.

wv.upstream: http://wvware.sourceforge.net/ (dead since ~2010; original abisource.com downloads are gone — tarball below is the canonical bits via a distro mirror)
vendored_paths: <flat library sources only: *.c/*.h at the dir root>
wv.dropped: converter mains (wvWare.c, wvText.in, wvConvert.c, wvRTF.c, wvSummary.c, wvVersion.c), helper scripts (wvHtml.in, wvLatex.in, wvPDF.in, wvPS.in, wvDVI.in, wvAbw.in, wvCleanLatex.in, wvDocBook.in, wvWml.in, wvMime), getopt.c/getopt1.c, patterns/, wingdingfont/, xml/, help/, GNUmakefile.*, autotools machinery, version.c.in, wv-1.0.pc.in, README, NEWS
wv.notes: Upstream is dead; this tree carries a large local security/correctness patch set from the DOC01-23 + UB/SEC/MEM audit series (see git history, task notes in .devin/TASKS.md). 'Upgrading' means a 3-way merge: regenerate the patch series with `tools/vendor-check.py --patch-out DIR wv` against a new upstream drop, or treat the vendored tree as effectively maintained in-tree.
